questions.text: Define an analytic (holomorphic) function on an open set.
State the Cauchy–Riemann equations and the theorem that relates them to differentiability.
Prove that if f = u + iv is analytic, then u and v are harmonic functions.
Evaluate the contour integral of 1/(z^2 + 1) around |z| = 2 using residues.
Why must the Cauchy–Riemann equations hold at a point for a function to be complex differentiable there, and why is that not sufficient on its own?
Every analytic function is infinitely differentiable — explain why this has no real-variable analogue.
